question: Who was appointed as Secretary of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Santosh Kumar Sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Santosh Kumar Sarangi**, a senior IAS officer, was appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) in April 2025.
 
• He is an IAS officer of the Odisha cadre and has served in various capacities in both state and central government.
 
• The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is the nodal ministry for formulating policies and programs related to renewable energy such as solar, wind, biomass, and small hydro resources.
 
• The appointment comes at a time when India is pushing aggressively towards achieving its renewable energy targets, including its commitment to achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.
 
• Santosh Kumar Sarangi's leadership is expected to guide the ministry in scaling up renewable energy projects and ensuring India’s energy transition aligns with its environmental goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abhishek Singh**

 
 
• Abhishek Singh is an IAS officer who has served in various administrative roles but has not been appointed as the Secretary of MNRE.
 
• He is known for his involvement in technology-driven governance and public service initiatives.
 
• His expertise lies in digital transformation and e-governance projects in India.
 
 
 
• **Rajesh Kumar Sinha**
 
 
• Rajesh Kumar Sinha is an IAS officer who has held important administrative positions but is not associated with the MNRE in this context.
 
• He has served in other capacities related to governance and policy-making at the state or central level.
 
 
 
• **KK Pathak**
 
 
• KK Pathak, another senior IAS officer, has been involved in administrative services but does not hold the position of Secretary of MNRE.
 
• His contributions are significant in other areas of governance and public administration.
 
 
 
• **About the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**
 
 
• The MNRE is responsible for planning and implementing India’s renewable energy programs and policies.
 
• It focuses on achieving energy security, reducing carbon emissions, and promoting sustainable development.
 
• The ministry is instrumental in the deployment of renewable energy technologies such as solar power, wind energy, biomass, and small hydroelectric power projects.
 
• India’s renewable energy target includes achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, with significant contributions from MNRE initiatives.
